profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is a Yahoo data center in the La Vista area of Sarpy County, Nebraska, part of the same Omaha area data center corridor that has also drawn facilities from Travelers Insurance, Google, and other large operators. Data Center Knowledge and Data Center Dynamics both covered the Nebraska facility opening and later expansion in trade press, and regional contractors including Cupertino Electric and a local roofing contractor have documented their own work on the project. Corporately, Yahoo has changed ownership more than once in recent years, having operated as Verizon Media following Verizon earlier acquisition of Yahoo core business, then sold to Apollo Global Management, with the transaction closing September 1, 2021 and Yahoo continuing afterward as a standalone company under Apollo Funds, with Verizon retaining a ten percent stake. No specific critical IT megawattage figure for this facility was found published from a tier one Yahoo owned source, though trade press describes it as a large scale internet services data center supporting Yahoo search, mail, and media products. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
Yahoo's power consumption at its Nebraska data center remains undisclosed, limiting visibility into how much compute capacity supports its search, mail, and media products from that location.

The facility sits within the Omaha-area data center corridor, which has attracted multiple large operators including Google and Travelers Insurance. This clustering suggests the region offers advantages for data center deployment, though the data does not specify whether those are power availability, grid capacity, real estate costs, or proximity to users. Yahoo's presence there is confirmed through trade press coverage of the facility's opening and expansion, plus documentation from regional contractors who performed work on the project.

Yahoo's corporate ownership has shifted substantially. Verizon acquired Yahoo's core business, operated it as Verizon Media, then sold it to Apollo Global Management in September 2021. Yahoo now operates as a standalone company under Apollo Funds while Verizon retained a ten percent stake. This ownership history makes it difficult to assess long-term commitment to the Nebraska facility or plans for capacity growth there. The lack of published megawattage data from Yahoo means the site cannot quantify how this facility contributes to the company's overall compute infrastructure or how it ranks against other data center operators in the region.
